handoff.summary: Scope revision only: spherical-interface-imaging@r2 uses curvature to include the separately sourced plane apparent-depth boundary while preserving both curved signs, index matching and finite-image singularities. Eighteen nonduplicate scientific relationships remain; no extra model coverage is counted for a special case.

assumptions: Source assumption: one refracting interface and paraxial rays; for a plane boundary, the apparent-depth relation is the near-normal viewing approximation, not arbitrary oblique viewing.
Source geometry: medium 2 continues without a subsequent refracting interface; both supplied phase indices correspond to the same optical frequency and declared medium states.
Source/profile convention: real-is-positive conjugates and a finite real object d_o>0; signed surface curvature follows the outgoing-center-positive convention.
Application profile: ordinary transparent real-index media n_1,n_2>=1. Equal indices and zero curvature are explicitly admitted no-refraction/plane limits; no default material values.

gaps: Add/use signed_optical_surface_curvature and coherent 1/m (same sign convention as b02 thin-lens-maker); use the proposed phase_refractive_index and conjugate-distance meanings. Units m and 1 exist; 1/m remains a research extension.

Revision r2 replaces finite R input with C=1/R and supports C=0. Existing instances need explicit radius-to-curvature mapping; zero radius must never map to zero curvature. Preserve plane near-normal viewing and distinguish axial apparent depth from transverse image height.

models.inverse_notes: Solve d_o=n_1*d_i/[(n_2-n_1)*C*d_i-n_2] given n_1,n_2>=1, finite C and d_i!=0; require displayed denominator!=0, reconstructed d_o>0 and original forward guards. Solve C=(n_1*d_i+n_2*d_o)/[(n_2-n_1)*d_o*d_i] given d_o>0,d_i!=0,n_1,n_2>=1,n_2!=n_1; C=0 is individually admissible, and original finite-image guard must hold. Example (n_1,n_2,C,d_o,d_i)=(1,1.5,10,0.4,0.6) reconstructs d_o=0.4 and C=10; original reciprocal equation gives 2.5+2.5=5. Plane example (1.5,1,0,0.3,-0.2) reconstructs C=0 and d_o=0.3; forward gives -0.2. If n_1=n_2 and d_i=-d_o, every finite C (including plane C=0) is compatible and curvature is underdetermined; other conjugates inconsistent. A zero image distance is unavailable for a finite nonzero real object. Recovering a finite spherical R=1/C additionally requires C!=0; plane C=0 means R infinite, not R=0. All non-singular mentioned inverses have one root; refractive-index inversions not separately assessed.
limitations: No second surface or complete thick-lens/sphere system is included; a later interface needs separate modeling.
An object at the curved-interface first focus produces parallel transmitted rays and no finite d_i.
Plane-interface apparent depth depends on viewing angle outside the near-normal/paraxial regime; Eq. 2.10 is not asserted as exact at arbitrary angles.
No image intensity, transmission fraction, group delay, diffraction or polarization prediction is provided.

references.method: Independent small-angle ray geometry at height h=0.001 m: incoming slope=h/0.4=0.0025; local normal slope=-h/0.1=-0.010. Incident relative-normal angle 0.0125 becomes 0.00833333333333 in index 1.5. Outgoing slope -0.00166666666667 reaches the axis after 0.001/0.00166666666667=0.6 m. Oracle uses refraction and ray intersection, not serialized conjugate equation. Synthetic paraxial values, tolerance covers repeating decimals. For r2 the same physical radius is supplied as introduced curvature C=1/R; expected and tolerance are unchanged.

Backward extension reaches axis at -0.001/0.005=-0.2 m. Exact synthetic small-angle data; 1e-12 m floating-point allowance. This is a virtual location of the unchanged object rather than a new real focus. For r2 the same physical radius is supplied as introduced curvature C=1/R; expected and tolerance are unchanged.

references.method: Independent synthetic near-normal ray construction: object depth 0.300 m in index 1.5, plane interface, outgoing medium index 1. At lateral surface intercept 0.001 m the incident slope magnitude is 0.001/0.300=1/300; the source's paraxial boundary geometry gives outgoing slope 1.5/300=0.005. Back-projecting 0.001/0.005 gives positive apparent depth 0.200 m on the incident side, hence signed d_i=-0.200 m. This uses the plane ray/apparent-depth construction, not serialized curved-conjugate replay; tolerance covers exact synthetic decimal arithmetic.

rejection_cases.reason: At the curved-interface first object focus, transmitted rays are parallel and the finite-image denominator vanishes.
A real object on the interface is excluded by the original finite-conjugate real-object domain; C=0 alone is valid and is not rejected.
Surface curvature is required; do not silently assume a plane when the geometry is unspecified.

relationship.locator: University Physics 3 section 2.3 Eqs. 2.10 and 2.11, plane normal-view paragraph and single-surface sign convention
relationship.original_equation: n_1/d_o+n_2/d_i=(n_2-n_1)/R (Eq. 2.11); plane normal-view apparent depth h_i=(n_2/n_1)*h_o (Eq. 2.10)
relationship.translation_notes: Introduce signed geometric surface curvature C=1/R for finite nonzero spherical radius, with C=0 representing the plane boundary. Solve the unchanged Eq. 2.11 for d_i in curvature coordinates. Eq. 2.10 independently supports the plane limit: source apparent depth h_i is a positive distance on the incident side, so local d_i=-h_i and d_o=h_o; C=0 gives d_i=-(n_2/n_1)*d_o. Source h_i here is axial apparent depth, not the transverse image height used in magnification; do not bind those quantities by shared symbol. The old R!=0 exclusion becomes exclusion of infinite C (all scalar inputs must be finite), not C!=0. Thus admitting C=0 does not silently restore the original forbidden R=0. Dimensions: numerator L, denominator (1)*(L^-1)*L-1=1, output L. m and coherent research 1/m avoid inlined unit conversion. Normal-view/paraxial source approximations remain explicit; no new approximation of a forbidden angle law is authored.

sources.evidence: Section 2.3 supplies both the index-weighted spherical conjugate law and the near-normal plane apparent-depth law. Signed curvature extends the same conjugate relationship to the plane limit, after converting the positive axial apparent depth to a negative virtual-image distance. The source's h_i in the plane passage is an axial depth, not transverse image height.
